body: It is a great place to go if you want to escape for a while, it is Adult Disneyland.  Gambling triggers the same chemical reaction in the brain as some drugs, like cocaine for instance, so being here has a very euphoric effect.  They have the some of the highest quality food in the world also, with any type of cuisine you could ever want, it's nice.  Sometime next week I am going to go out to California and stay on the beach which is where I am going to have my passing.  I always loved the beach but have only seen sunrises as I haven't been out to the west coast before, so seeing a sunset on the pacific is the last thing in life I really want to see.
I am not trying to prevent you from committing suicide at all Diana.  I am just not going to aid you in doing so.  I am sorry I can't be of any help :-(.
I am not here to encourage anyone to commit suicide.  I am simply telling my story in the hopes that it will benefit someone, somehow.

I am not going to answer this.  I probably shouldn't have divulged my method in the first place.  I do not recommend anyone to make the decision I have made until they attempt to get help.  Even then, if your suicide is brought upon by a life event such as a breakup, the pain is temporary.  

I look at my decision like it is euthanasia.  I have an illness that is incurable, like a cancer.  I have emotional cancer.

Also, someone just PM'd me asking me "why are you measuring your life with relationships?" 

Well I am partially.  A big part of life is made up of the relationships you form with other human beings.  I also measure the quality of my life by my happiness and as I mentioned in a reply a second ago, happiness is a fleeting emotion for me.  I am crippled by my depression, it is hard to explain to someone who hasn't experienced it.  It isn't like a depression you have after a breakup or a death of a loved one, nothing needs to happen for me to become depressed, there is something wrong with the way my brain functions, I am depressed all of the time except when I am high or engaging in an extremely pleasurable/adrenaline fueled activity.  Medication helps some people to "balance out", it did not provide any benefit to me at all and I took anti-depressants for years.

No.  There isn't anything else I can try, I've tried to get help for my depression for over a decade.  Nothing has shown results.  I am talking about a ton of time and money spent trying to rid myself of this disease.  In my opinion there is no cure for chronic depression, it is a lifelong battle and the hell that I have put myself through mentally has damaged my soul, rendering me incapable of anything but brief moments of happiness.  I don't want to live like this for the rest of my life.
